The normal CA-125 level is an important clue, as it often points toward a benign condition or a specific syndrome rather than epithelial ovarian cancer. I need to visualize the mass and check for fluid accumulation, so I will request an ultrasound and a chest X-ray to evaluate for pleural effusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The triad of a large ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion is classic for Meigs' syndrome, especially given the normal CA-125 level which makes malignancy less likely. I need to confirm if this is a benign fibroma, so I will request medical images to better characterize the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of systemic symptoms like fever or night sweats, along with the classic triad of ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with a normal CA-125, strongly supports a diagnosis of Meigs' syndrome.
